title: A concept is renamed by a version of its own kind; a concept is its versions joined by supersession or a shared name
situation: 0318 realized renaming. Its code review found that joined lines of work, one renaming a concept to a name the other defines, fold differently by entry order and can leave a concept no verb reaches; that a close of competing versions naming a concept differently had no settled form; and that a runtime predating renaming, reading past the rename, still files later versions of the concept under its new name, so it shows both names live.
decision: As 0318, with (1), (2), (5) and (6) restated. (1) supersede takes an optional rename, the name the concept takes from this version on. A version given one is an entry of its own kind, rename: everything a supersede carries, its name the new one, plus was, the name it renames. A runtime that predates it reads it past and says its answer may be incomplete (0297); what such a runtime shows of the concept afterwards is not relied on. (2) A concept is the versions of one context joined by supersession or by a shared name, whatever the order they were recorded in, so a define and a rename that give one name on joined lines are versions of one concept, competing, as two defines of one name are. Its name is its current version's: state and design show it under that name only; history, named by any name it has had, lists every version, each with the name it was recorded under and its reason. Every verb naming a concept takes its current name or an earlier one. (3) and (4) as 0318. (5) While current versions compete and name the concept differently, it is listed among the competing under the name of the latest version they all supersede, else the earliest version's, each competing version showing the name it gives; a later version settles them as for any concept. (6) Closing the books opens a renamed concept as a define under its current name, writing every opening's built-from with each reference's current name; its earlier names stay in the closed period. A close is refused, changing nothing, while a concept's current versions name it differently, naming the concept and the remedy: settle them with supersede first.
consequences: Supersedes 0318. The fold is the same whatever order joined entries sort in. A close never carries an earlier name into a new period. One builder; review Ask.
